claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and drop an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, before it ever starts.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue, with each running in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The AWS CodePipeline user guide 'how it works' concepts page documents the execution modes.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on the environment targeted by a deployment job, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` can be set on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
In Azure Pipelines, the default value of `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
In TeamCity, the build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' is located under the build configuration's General Settings (as an advanced option).
With TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as a page on update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments to that stack.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior: sequential` can be set on a stage to make runs queue behind an exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting, and setting it to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1 prevents concurrent deployments.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
